value: This article defines a monoid as an algebraic structure comprising a set equipped with an associative binary operation and an identity element, effectively a semigroup with an identity. It explores monoids through various common examples, such as nonnegative integers under addition, strings under concatenation, and functions under composition. Key properties, including submonoids, invertible elements (which form a group), and commutative monoids, are examined, alongside monoid homomorphisms and their equational presentations. The text further highlights the wide-ranging significance of monoids across mathematics, particularly their foundational role in category theory as single-object categories, and in computer science for applications in automata theory, formal language theory, and paradigms like MapReduce.
